description: Machine-readable source of truth for EngineOS risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, router escalation, repair-loop, circuit-breaker and telemetry policy — eleven blocks (risk, autonomy, gates, parallelism, retry, prompt_signals, router, repair, breaker, hitl, telemetry), added across P1 (risk/autonomy/gates/parallelism/retry) through P7 (telemetry). rules/risk-autonomy.md, rules/gates.md and rules/parallelism.md stay the human-readable mirror and are not edited to match. scripts/validate-engineos.sh checks this file: C16 extracts prose numbers (wave cap, retry attempts/escalations, spec threshold) and enum tables and compares them against this file; C17 checks prompt_signals; C18 checks the router block; C20 checks repair; C22 checks telemetry; C24 checks parallelism.backpressure (the dispatch loop's admission control, answered by kernel.sh admit and mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Backpressure'); C25 checks breaker (the per-resource circuit breaker, answered by kernel.sh breaker and mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'); C26 checks hitl (human-in-the-loop as a queryable entity, answered by kernel.sh hitl, folded into resolve-task as .hitl, and mirrored in rules/risk-autonomy.md 'Human-in-the-loop'); C27 checks telemetry.exec_journal (the agent-span journal, written by the hooks through src/hooks/telemetry.ts's span lifecycle and mirrored in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces'), C28 the retrieval-metrics reference and its RAG mirror, and C29 the adoption entrypoint wiring — so a future prose edit or block change that diverges fails CI.

inputs.low: Trivially undone, e.g. a git revert.
inputs.high: Irreversible, or reversible only with data loss.
Production, other teams, or external consumers.
PII, credentials, financial, or clinical data.
Public/published API, DB schema, or event payload.

levels.permitted: Recommend, draft, or propose a diff — do not apply it.
Apply reversible changes in the working tree.
Apply, but a human gate precedes any external effect.
Bounded autonomous operation, monitored, with a kill switch.

backpressure.note: Admission control for the orchestrator's dispatch loop. Capacity is wave_concurrency_cap above (never a second copy). Answered by scripts/kernel.sh admit; mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Backpressure'. defer = hold the unit for the next wave; reject = stop planning, report BLOCKED, re-plan with a human (a hitl reason).

prompt_signals.note: Prompt-classification EREs for kernel.sh scale (were hardcoded in the UserPromptSubmit advisor before the kernel owned them). Countable nouns in scale are plural-only on purpose: 'add a component' is one unit and must not trip fan-out advice. design_weak only counts alongside an action verb.

repair.note: Check-level failure policy: what to do when a validation check is red during a fix loop. The agent-unit counterpart is the retry block; both encode the same bound discipline (rules/parallelism.md: two attempts, one escalation, then a human) over different failure kinds — an agent unit reports an envelope status, a check exits nonzero. Read by scripts/kernel.sh repair, and in-process by src/hooks/stop-verify.ts, which asks src/kernel/repair for the whole section and renders the reason it answers rather than reading these numbers itself. The numeric agreement with retry is evidence-based, not law: if P7 telemetry ever justifies a different check bound, this block changes and nothing else does.

breaker.note: Resource-level failure policy — the third failure block, and deliberately not a variant of the other two. retry asks "try this UNIT again?" and counts attempts against an agent envelope status; repair asks "fix this CHECK again?" and counts attempts against a nonzero exit; breaker asks "why are we still calling this RESOURCE?" — one of the scopes below: provider, mcp, tool or agent — and counts consecutive failures against the resource itself. Folding it into retry would tie a per-unit attempt counter to a per-resource health signal, so every fresh unit would rediscover a dead dependency from attempt one. Consult breaker BEFORE retry. Read by scripts/kernel.sh breaker, which is the transition table and nothing more: the orchestrator owns the state and the consecutive-failure count, taken from the exec journal (span_kind tool or model, status FAILED, same tool/provider). scopes is advisory: it is the orchestrator's vocabulary for keying a breaker's state per resource, and no kernel code path reads it, so C25a's non-empty check and C25c's prose grep are the only things holding those ids to the frozen contract. Mirrored in rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'; scripts/validate-engineos.sh C25 checks the block, the kernel's transitions and the prose together. ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-03-circuit-breaker-separate-from-retry.md.

hitl.note: Human-in-the-loop as a queryable entity rather than a tier's implication. autonomy.ceiling_by_risk says how far a unit may go alone; this block says when a HUMAN must decide and names WHY, so the decision is auditable instead of inferred. Answered by scripts/kernel.sh hitl, folded into resolve-task as .hitl from a CLASSIFIED tier only (decision_rules.any_high) and never from a risk floor, because a floor is an input to classification and a gate announced off one is gate theatre (rules/gates.md); on a floor-only prompt .hitl is null and src/hooks/prompt-advisor.ts turns task_contract.risk_floor into an instruction to classify rather than a gate, announced by src/hooks/prompt-advisor.ts, mirrored in rules/risk-autonomy.md 'Human-in-the-loop'; C26 checks the block, the kernel's answers and the prose together. reasons is the CLOSED vocabulary a gate may cite — a gate citing anything else produces a record no one can argue with, which is the hole this block exists to close; the list order is the kernel's emission order. situations is what --situation accepts ON TOP OF retry.never_retry (whose ids all collapse to the single reason never-retry-situation), and the two lists are disjoint so the union lookup stays unambiguous. budget-exhausted is deliberately in BOTH reasons and situations: it is a reason a human is needed AND a situation a caller reports, and kernel.sh admit's reject message embeds the literal 'hitl: budget-exhausted' — C26d couples that literal to this list and to the kernel's own --situation reject answer so the three cannot drift apart. autonomy_after is a DROP and never a raise: one level below the ceiling passed in, no lower than A1, capped at risk high by autonomy.high_with_thin_evidence, and never above the level given -- so A0 stays A0. record_home is where the decision gets written down; a tier that required a human and carries no such record has not passed its gate. ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-03-hitl-as-kernel-entity.md.

telemetry.note: Kernel-decision event capture: which routes, decision rules and verifications actually fired, as ids and outcomes only — never prompt text (value_pattern has no whitespace class; scripts/telemetry.sh rejects on append and validate). Written by src/hooks/prompt-advisor.ts and src/hooks/stop-verify.ts to $GITDIR/engineos-telemetry/<session_id>.jsonl in the consumer project, only where .engineos/ exists (the scaffolder's own opt-in gate) and ENGINEOS_TELEMETRY is not 0. Read by skills/retro (step 1) and scripts/usage-report.sh; reaped by src/hooks/ensure-project-layout.ts after retention_days. Events live in .git and never reach CI — validate-engineos.sh C22 checks this policy and the plumbing, never the data. written_by is an array because one event can have several writers, which supersedes the one-writer-per-event shape recorded in docs/specs/2026-08-06-decision-kernel-p7-telemetry.md. The samples are asserted by C22b against the running telemetry.sh, the self-validating-registry pattern of routing.json's sample_path and router.fixtures. Attempt-level repair/retry outcomes are deliberately absent: no hook mediates those model-invoked kernel calls, and their designed home is the exec-journal schema, written by the ai-se-os runner follow-on.

exec_journal.note: Agent-span capture: what actually HAPPENED when agents ran, as the counterpart to the events above, which record what EngineOS DECIDED. One session is one trace (trace_id = session_id) and every dispatched agent, router decision and verification gate is a span in it; span_kinds is the closed vocabulary, the closed vocabulary, resolved directly from here by src/journal/schema.ts, so there is no second copy to rename apart. The schema is scripts/exec-journal.sh, whose v2 span fields are all OPTIONAL: a v1 line carries none of the keys and stays valid, and backward compatibility is the contract. Containment, stated the same way here, in scripts/exec-journal.sh's header and in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces': every field EXCEPT note is a slug matching the same telemetry.value_pattern above, and the validator rejects a line where one of them is not; note is the only field that admits FREE TEXT, but it is NOT the only field carrying attacker-influenced content and a consumer must not treat it as the single untrusted field: a harness-supplied value transits dash-joined through hookSlug, so its characters still reach disk, and the value_pattern slug class admits '.' and '/' -- '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' is a valid slug that exec-journal.sh validate passes clean. A journal field is therefore NEVER safe as a filesystem path component; a consumer building a path from one narrows it itself, and src/lib/slug.ts's hookPathSlug (the same class minus '.' and '/') is that narrowing. The two boundaries differ on purpose and the difference is the whole claim: the CLI REJECTS a value that is not a slug, while the hooks SANITIZE first (hookSlug maps every other character to '-') so that a span is recorded rather than lost. So a harness-supplied value's characters still transit, dash-joined -- 'SECRET=hunter2 x' lands as 'SECRET-hunter2-x'. What the guard buys is that no field but note can carry whitespace, a newline, a quote or a control character, so nothing written through one can break the line format, smuggle a second JSON object or span two lines, and every value is length-bounded. It bounds the SHAPE and the SIZE of what reaches disk; it does not classify the content. Every value, note included, is capped at max_value_length characters on append, and over-long is a reject rather than a truncation. An earlier version claimed there was no free-text field at all while run_id, capability_id and agent accepted one, which is the shape of claim this registry must not carry. Adding another free-text field is a compatibility event (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), never a convenience. Written by the hooks in written_by through src/hooks/telemetry.ts's span lifecycle; the agent span is a PAIR, where announce-agent-dispatch.ts writes only the start marker (a PreToolUse and its PostToolUse are separate processes, so the start instant has to survive on disk) and announce-agent-return.sh writes the line, which is why both are listed. All of it runs under the same opt-in gates as the events: only where .engineos/ exists, only when ENGINEOS_TELEMETRY is not 0, never in a bypassed session. Those hooks see no model usage, so agent spans carry tokens_in/tokens_out 0 and no cost_micros at all; a 0 there means unknown, never free. tool and model spans, real token counts and real costs come from a headless runner that owns the model call and does not exist yet. Reaped by src/hooks/ensure-project-layout.ts on telemetry.retention_days -- the '*.jsonl' glob already covers <session>.exec.jsonl. Consumed by the breaker's consecutive-failure count (rules/parallelism.md 'Circuit breaker'), which needs a status source that actually observes failure: the dispatch hooks' status is a FLOOR on that count, since a structured tool_response with no error flag reads as OK. Mirrored in rules/observability.md 'Agent traces'; C27 checks the block, the running CLI and the prose together.

router.note: Escalation policy for the P3 router agent: when the deterministic kernel answer is not enough and a model must produce a dispatch plan. Read by scripts/kernel.sh route-escalate; the fixtures are asserted by validate-engineos.sh C18e and scripts/test-kernel.sh.
